titleEn: Assault With Traumatic Brain Injury - Declining GCS

patient.name: Ryan Kowalski
patient.affectEn: lying on his left side on the wet grass, moaning; blood in the hair over the right temple; vomit on the grass beside him; eyes open only when spoken to; confused and restless, keeps asking for his bag
patient.speechEn: confused, halting speech ('where... where is... my bag'); obeys simple commands slowly; cannot give a reliable history - police, the witness and his wife (by phone) supply the facts. After the decline (state change): eyes open only to pain, still confused words, no longer follows commands

scene.settingEn: Park pathway in Abbotsford at 2320 hrs. Dark - lit by police flashlights and your scene lights. Wet grass, 9 degrees C, light rain. Police have detained the assailant and secured a baseball bat as evidence; officers remain with you. The patient lies on his left side on the grass where he fell; a bystander rolled him there because he vomited. One patient.
hazardsEn: darkness - work under scene lights and police flashlights
wet, slippery grass, 9 degrees C and light rain - cold exposure for the patient
assault scene - assailant detained by police and the bat secured as evidence; police remain with you

bystanders.knowsEn: He was struck once on the right side of the head with a baseball bat about 15 minutes ago (around 2305) and fell backwards onto the grass. Witnesses say he was knocked out for roughly 2 minutes, then woke up confused and has vomited twice. No other blows were seen. The assailant is detained and the bat is secured. Can phone his wife for his medical history if asked, and can hold lights or help carry under your direction.

Saw the single blow; he went down and was out for about 2 minutes; when he came round he was confused and vomited, so she rolled him onto his left side; he has vomited twice in total; she has not moved him since.
Nothing significant medically; he takes no medications and is NOT on any blood thinners (anticoagulants); no known allergies; no diabetes; he has been fit and well.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: spinal immobilization device (spine board or scoop stretcher)
hard cervical collars in all adult sizes
head blocks (foam rollers) and spinal straps
portable suction unit with rigid tip
oxygen kit with nasal cannula and non-rebreather mask
PCP only: IV start kit with normal saline

dispatchEn: 2320 hrs. Code 3 to a park pathway in Abbotsford. 38-year-old male assaulted, struck in the head with a baseball bat. Police are on scene and have detained the assailant. Trauma centre is 20 minutes away; the local hospital is 8 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: witnesses say he was knocked out and is now awake but 'not making sense'. Police confirm the scene is safe.
arrivalEn: A police officer meets you on the dark park pathway with a flashlight: "He took one swing from a bat to the head. We've got the guy who did it and the bat's secured - the scene's safe." Wet grass, light rain, 9 degrees C, your scene lights on. The patient lies on his left side on the grass with vomit beside him; a bystander stands nearby. One patient.
firstLookEn: A 38-year-old man lying on his left side on the wet grass, moaning, with blood in the hair over his right temple and vomit on the grass beside him.

primary.locEn: Eyes open to your voice (AVPU = V). Confused speech: "where... where is... my bag". Obeys simple commands slowly. A decreased LOC. (After the decline state change: eyes open only to pain, speech still confused, localizes to pain but no longer obeys commands.)
primary.airwayEn: Vomit in the mouth - the airway needs SUCTION (10-15 seconds at a time in an adult) and ongoing monitoring because he may vomit again. Once suctioned: clear and patent. He is talking, gag reflex intact.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 14, regular, adequate depth, equal chest rise.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 58, strong and bounding. Slow venous bleeding from a right temporal scalp wound.
primary.rbsEn: 6 cm boggy swelling and laceration over the right temporal scalp with slow venous bleeding that controls with direct pressure; no depressed skull fracture felt; no CSF from the ears or nose; no other injuries - chest, abdomen, pelvis, back and all four limbs unremarkable. Skin is given automatically during the RBS: pale, warm, dry. He is lying on his left side on cold, wet grass in light rain.

history.ccEn: My head... it hurts. Where... where is my bag?

opqrst.oEn: (Confused) "I don't... what happened?" Police and the witness: struck once on the right side of the head with a baseball bat about 15 minutes ago.
opqrst.tEn: (Confused) "I don't know how long." Witnesses: since the blow, about 15 minutes ago.

history.painScoreEn: "My head hurts... maybe six?" - an unreliable score because of his confusion.

sample.sEn: "My head hurts." Witnesses: knocked out for about 2 minutes, confused since, and he has vomited twice.
sample.aEn: Patient: "I... don't know." His wife, by phone through police: no known allergies.
sample.mEn: Patient: "No..." His wife, by phone: he takes no medications.
sample.pEn: Patient cannot answer reliably. His wife, by phone: nothing significant, and he is NOT on any blood thinners (anticoagulants).
sample.eEn: Patient: "I don't remember." Police and the witness: struck once on the right side of the head with a baseball bat about 15 minutes ago; fell backwards onto the grass; knocked out for roughly 2 minutes; awake but confused since; vomited twice; no other blows seen; a bystander rolled him onto his left side because he vomited.

fe.generalEn: His wife, by phone: fit, no recent illness. (He cannot answer reliably.)
fe.cnsEn: "My head hurts." Witnesses: knocked out for about 2 minutes, confused since; no seizure seen.
fe.respiratoryEn: "No..." - nothing reported by witnesses or his wife.
fe.cardiovascularEn: "No..." - nothing reported by witnesses or his wife.
fe.integumentaryEn: The cut on the right side of his head; nothing else.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: "No..." - no other injuries reported or found.
fe.endocrineEn: His wife, by phone: no diabetes.
fe.eentEn: "Things looked blurry... before." No fluid from his ears or nose.

findings.headNeckEn: 6 cm right temporal laceration with boggy swelling; bleeding controlled by direct pressure; no depression palpable; no CSF from the ears or nose; no Battle sign or raccoon eyes yet. No midline cervical tenderness elicited, but he is an unreliable patient.
findings.chestLungsEn: Clear and equal at all 6 sites. No injury.
findings.backEn: Checked during the roll onto the device: no injury.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: Moves both legs to command; no injury. (After the decline he no longer follows commands.)
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Moves both arms; grip equal; no injury. (After the decline he no longer follows commands; he localizes to pain.)

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: baseline on scene (SpO2 becomes 98% once oxygen is applied - see state change oxygen-applied)
vitalsSets.pupils: UNEQUAL - right 5 mm sluggish, left 3 mm brisk

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: deteriorating (rising ICP) from 12 minutes, normally en route; unlocks together with state change gcs-decline. SpO2 is patched by the oxygen / assisted-ventilation state changes
vitalsSets.pupils: right 6 mm non-reactive, left 3 mm reactive

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: The patient is changing. He no longer opens his eyes when you speak to him - only to a painful stimulus. His words are still confused, and he no longer follows commands but reaches toward a painful stimulus. His breathing has slowed and is becoming irregular.

vitalsPatch.pupils: right 6 mm non-reactive, left 3 mm reactive

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan spinal equipment, oxygen, BVM, suction, and a rapid trauma-centre transport
triggers: plan for oxygen and airway management
this will be a trauma centre transport

expected.actionEn: Anticipate a head injury with altered LOC - plan for airway compromise and vomiting
Verbalize hazards (dark, wet, cold, assault scene - police present), environment, MOI (blunt head trauma with bat), one patient
triggers: it's dark, get the scene lights on
mechanism is a bat to the head

expected.actionEn: Don gloves and eye protection (blood and vomit)
First look: patient on his side, moaning, blood in the hair on the right temple, vomit beside him
triggers: blood in his hair on the right side

expected.actionEn: Protect from the environment: get the patient off the cold wet ground promptly and shield from rain
triggers: get him off the wet ground
get him into the ambulance out of the cold

expected.actionEn: Assess LOC / AVPU: responds to Voice, confused - a decreased LOC
Take manual c-spine control immediately - blunt head trauma with altered LOC is a NEXUS-positive indication
Assess the airway and SUCTION the vomit; keep the airway clear throughout
Consider and correctly size an airway adjunct (OPA only if the gag reflex is absent; NPA is an option if not contraindicated)
triggers: he has a gag reflex so no OPA

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing rate and adequacy; be ready to assist ventilations if the rate falls
Assess circulation - recognize bradycardia with a bounding pulse as a possible rising-ICP sign
Complete the RBS; control scalp bleeding with direct pressure; palpate for depressed skull fracture and check ears/nose for fluid
triggers: direct pressure on the scalp wound
feel for a depressed skull fracture
check the ears and nose for fluid

expected.actionEn: Note skin: pale warm dry
Apply oxygen to keep SpO2 at or above 94% - TBI patients must not be allowed to desaturate
triggers: SpO2 is 93 so he needs oxygen

expected.actionEn: Manage position: spinal precautions with the head of the bed elevated 30 degrees once packaged, and airway protection given the vomiting
triggers: head of the bed up 30 degrees
keep him on his side to protect the airway

expected.actionEn: Categorize as RTC and act with urgency
Packaged and ready to load within 15 minutes with the airway managed
Verbalize the trauma-centre destination decision and notify early
triggers: go to the trauma centre not the local hospital

expected.actionEn: Establish chief complaint: head injury with altered mental status
HxC/C from witnesses: number of blows, weapon, duration of LOC, vomiting, behaviour since, any lucid interval
triggers: how many times was he hit
how has he been acting since
did he wake up and then get worse

expected.actionEn: Pain score if obtainable; document that reliability is limited by confusion
PMHx from family/police - specifically anticoagulant use
Medications
Allergies
LOI including alcohol
GCS with all three components and the correct total (E3 V4 M6 = 13, moderate TBI)
BP by auscultation - recognize hypertension with a widening pulse pressure
Pulse - recognize bradycardia with a bounding character
Respirations rate/depth/character; watch for irregular patterns
Skin hands-on
Pupils - identify and act on the unequal, sluggish right pupil; repeat with every set
SpO2 with calibration; keep at or above 94%
BGL - indicated with any altered LOC
Temperature - indicated after exposure on cold wet ground
triggers: he's been on the cold ground

expected.actionEn: FE - General health (from witnesses/family)
FE - CNS (pertinent: LOC duration, headache, seizure, vision)
FE - Respiratory
FE - Cardiovascular
FE - GI/GU (vomiting is a TBI red flag)
triggers: how many times has he vomited

expected.actionEn: FE - Integumentary
FE - Musculoskeletal
FE - Endocrine
FE - EENT (vision, ear/nose discharge)
Head/neck exam: DOTS, skull depression, CSF from ears/nose, Battle sign, raccoon eyes
Chest exam with 6-site auscultation
Abdomen exam
Back exam during the roll
triggers: check the back during the roll
log roll and check the back

expected.actionEn: Lower extremities with motor and sensory check
triggers: can you feel me touch your legs

expected.actionEn: Upper extremities with grip strength comparison
Maintain oxygenation at or above 94% and be prepared to assist ventilations without routine hyperventilation
Elevate the head of the bed 30 degrees and loosen the hard collar after securing
triggers: elevate the head of the bed 30 degrees
loosen the hard collar once he's secured

expected.actionEn: Spinal packaging performed correctly (collar, device, body before head, no head tape)
triggers: secure the body first then the head

expected.actionEn: Airway management: suction correctly (10-15 seconds adult), adjunct sized and inserted appropriately, patient positioned to protect against aspiration
Do NOT administer TXA - contraindicated in isolated TBI
triggers: TXA is contraindicated in isolated TBI
TXA not indicated for head injury

expected.actionEn: PCP: IV TKVO with systolic above 120, and keep BGL between 4.0 and 8.0
Reassess ABCs and all interventions after each major move and after any change in LOC
Second full set of vitals within 5-6 minutes including a repeat GCS and pupils
Recognize the deteriorating GCS and pupil change and escalate care (assist ventilations, suction ready, urgent notification)
Assist ventilations at an appropriate rate with the BVM connected to oxygen, confirming chest rise
Urgent trauma-centre notification including GCS trend and unequal pupils
Complete hand-off with both GCS scores broken down by component
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate rolls, sits up or otherwise moves the patient, lets him lift or turn his head, or applies a painful stimulus before manual in-line c-spine control is established (he was found on his left side and may be suctioned in that position)

candidate (or the partner on the candidate's instruction) releases manual c-spine control before the patient is fully secured to the spinal device with body straps and head blocks; applying the collar alone does not permit release
candidate has been told there is vomit in the mouth and moves on to breathing, circulation, the RBS, vitals, history or packaging without suctioning or otherwise clearing it
candidate states a single suction pass of longer than 15 seconds
candidate inserts an oropharyngeal airway (OPA) while the patient is responding to voice with an intact gag reflex
after his breathing has been reported as slowing and becoming irregular (the decline), the candidate carries on with other tasks over the next turns without starting BVM-assisted ventilations
candidate ventilates at a deliberately fast rate or states that they will hyperventilate him to lower the intracranial pressure

after the examiner has described the decline (eyes only to pain, no longer obeying commands, breathing slowing), the candidate carries on with routine tasks (history, Functional Enquiry, head-to-toe) without reassessing his LOC/GCS, airway and breathing or escalating care
candidate tapes the patient's head to the spinal device
PCP gives a fluid bolus (runs normal saline wide open or orders a set volume such as 20 mL/kg or 500 mL); starting an IV with saline at TKVO is NOT this event

drugs.doseEn: 2 g (2000 mg) IV push over 1 minute in other trauma - CONTRAINDICATED here: isolated TBI. Withhold. Record drug:txa only if the candidate actually gives it.
IV TKVO while the systolic is above 120 mmHg (maintain systolic above 120); no fluid bolus - he is hypertensive
WITHHELD - contraindicated with an altered level of consciousness (head injury). Record drug:entonox only if the candidate actually gives it.
15 g PO - NOT indicated: BGL 5.6 mmol/L is within the 4.0-8.0 target and he cannot reliably maintain his own airway (vomiting, decreased LOC)
10-25 g (100-250 mL of 10% solution) IV for hypoglycemia - NOT indicated: BGL 5.6 mmol/L is within the 4.0-8.0 target

notificationFacts.cc: head injury with altered mental status - moderate TBI, deteriorating
notificationFacts.moi: assault at approximately 2305 - struck once to the right temple with a baseball bat, fell backwards onto grass
notificationFacts.hxcc: knocked out for about 2 minutes, confused since, vomited twice
notificationFacts.vitals: GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6), BP 168/92, pulse 58 bounding, resp 14, SpO2 93% on room air, right pupil 5 mm sluggish; now GCS 11 (E2 V4 M5), BP 178/88, pulse 52, resp 12 and irregular, right pupil 6 mm non-reactive
notificationFacts.treatments: airway suctioned, oxygen with ventilations now assisted, manual c-spine and full spinal packaging with the collar loosened and the head of the bed at 30 degrees, direct pressure to the scalp laceration; PCP: IV TKVO; no TXA; RTC to the trauma centre, ETA 20 minutes
notificationFacts.findings: 6 cm right temporal laceration with boggy swelling, no CSF, no palpable depression; signs of rising intracranial pressure

handoffFacts.cc: head injury with altered mental status
handoffFacts.moi: assaulted at approximately 2305, struck once to the right temple with a baseball bat, fell backwards onto grass
handoffFacts.hxcc: about 2 minutes of loss of consciousness, confused since, two episodes of vomiting; no other blows seen; lay on cold wet grass until our arrival
handoffFacts.initialVitals: GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6 - eyes to voice, confused, obeys commands), BP 168/92, pulse 58 strong bounding, resp 14 regular, skin pale warm dry, pupils unequal - right 5 mm sluggish, left 3 mm brisk, SpO2 93% on room air rising to 98% on oxygen, BGL 5.6 mmol/L, temperature 36.2 C
handoffFacts.finalVitals: GCS 11 (E2 V4 M5 - eyes to pain, confused, localizes), BP 178/88, pulse 52 bounding, resp 12 and becoming irregular, skin pale warm dry, right pupil 6 mm non-reactive, left 3 mm reactive, SpO2 97% on oxygen with assisted ventilations, BGL 5.6 mmol/L
handoffFacts.pmhx: no significant medical history (confirmed with his wife by phone); no anticoagulants
handoffFacts.treatments: vomit suctioned and airway maintained; oxygen to keep SpO2 at or above 94%, ventilations assisted once respirations slowed and became irregular, no hyperventilation; manual c-spine, hard collar and full spinal packaging, collar loosened after securing, head of the bed elevated 30 degrees; direct pressure to the scalp laceration; PCP: IV TKVO (systolic above 120); TXA withheld - contraindicated in isolated TBI; RTC to the trauma centre
handoffFacts.findings: 6 cm right temporal laceration with boggy swelling, bleeding controlled, no palpable depression, no CSF from the ears or nose, no Battle sign or raccoon eyes; GCS falling 13 to 11 with a dilating non-reactive right pupil, bradycardia and hypertension - signs of rising intracranial pressure; dinner at 1900 with two beers

pcrFacts.cc: Head injury with altered mental status after assault with a bat
pcrFacts.hxcc: Single blow to right temple ~2305, LOC approx 2 min, confused since, vomited twice; witnessed by police and bystanders
pcrFacts.pmhx: Nil significant; no anticoagulants (confirmed with spouse)
pcrFacts.vitals: Set 1 (on scene): GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6), BP 168/92, P 58 strong bounding, R 14 regular, skin pale warm dry, pupils R 5 mm sluggish / L 3 mm brisk, SpO2 93% RA then 98% on O2, BGL 5.6 mmol/L, temp 36.2 C. Set 2 (deteriorating): GCS 11 (E2 V4 M5), BP 178/88, P 52 bounding, R 12 becoming irregular, skin pale warm dry, pupils R 6 mm non-reactive / L 3 mm reactive, SpO2 97% on O2 with assisted ventilations, BGL 5.6 mmol/L
treatments: O2 titrated to SpO2 94% or above; assisted ventilations when resps fell
Manual c-spine, collar, full spinal packaging; collar loosened after securing
PCP: IV TKVO (SBP above 120); TXA withheld - contraindicated in isolated TBI
findings: Unequal pupils: R 5 mm sluggish then 6 mm non-reactive, L 3 mm reactive
Bradycardia 58 to 52 with hypertension 168/92 to 178/88 - Cushing pattern
6 cm right temporal laceration with boggy swelling; no CSF, no palpable depression

examinerPrompts.locNotDepictedEn: Volunteer whenever the candidate assesses LOC or GCS, because the actor cannot fully depict it. Before the decline: "He opens his eyes to your voice, his speech is confused, and he obeys simple commands slowly." Once the gcs-decline state change is in effect: "He no longer opens his eyes to your voice - only to a painful stimulus. His words are still confused. He no longer follows commands; he reaches toward a painful stimulus."
examinerPrompts.breathingNotDepictedEn: Once the gcs-decline state change is in effect, volunteer when the candidate assesses breathing: "His breathing has slowed and is becoming irregular." (The rate itself is spoken by the engine.)
examinerPrompts.missedInjuryEn: You examined his head during your rapid body survey - what did you find on the right side of his scalp?

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR: spinal packaging, suction, airway adjuncts, oxygenation at or above 94%, assisted ventilations, head of bed at 30 degrees, collar loosened, serial GCS and pupils, and rapid transport. No IV, no blood-sugar correction beyond recognizing the BGL (5.6 is normal). No Functional Enquiry. TXA is not in EMR scope and remains contraindicated regardless; Entonox is contraindicated (altered LOC).
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds IV TKVO (only if systolic is above 120 mmHg), maintenance of blood sugar between 4.0 and 8.0 mmol/L, maintenance of systolic above 120 mmHg, and the Functional Enquiry as far as the patient's confusion allows (no deduction for systems he cannot answer). TXA remains contraindicated in isolated TBI; no fluid bolus (hypertensive).

sourcePages: Scenario tr-06 (data/practical/scenarios.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing (deterioration to GCS 11), handoff, critical pitfalls. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (altered LOC is unstable); p.11 Primary survey interventions (c-spine stabilization when NEXUS/Canadian C-Spine indications are met; airway maintenance and suctioning with decreased LOC; assisting slow or failing respirations especially with decreasing LOC; oxygen for altered LOC and trauma); p.13 AVPU; p.25 Spinal Management (manual stabilization, hard collar, spinal immobilization device, foam blocks, secure the body, do not tape the head); p.27 Traumatic Brain Injuries (GCS 13 or more mild, 9-12 moderate, 8 or less severe; SpO2 94% or more, assist ventilations if needed keeping SpO2 at 94% or more; head of the bed at 30 degrees; loosen hard collar; PCP: BGL 4.0-8.0 mmol/L, systolic above 120 mmHg, IV TKVO if systolic is above 120; TXA contraindicated for isolated TBIs); p.57 Diabetic Emergencies and p.76 Oral Glucose (glucose only for BGL < 4.0; oral glucose only with sufficient mentation to maintain an airway); p.65 Entonox (contraindicated with altered level of consciousness); p.78 Tranexamic Acid (contraindicated in isolated TBIs).
